news.originalContent:
(Photo by Natalie Behring/Getty Images)

Industrial power users want federal regulators to force a regional grid operator to let competitors bid on four new power lines.

Southwest Power Pool (SPP) skipped competitive bidding on about $3.8 billion in transmission projects by wrongly labeling them short-term reliability fixes, the Electricity Transmission Competition Coalition and the Industrial Energy Consumers of America alleged in an Oct. 28 complaint to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). SPP’s answer is now due Dec. 17 after FERC pushed back the deadline, according to a Nov. 16 notice.

“By using the need date that cannot be met to preclude competition, SPP is losing the benefit of competition without a legitimate reason,” the coalition wrote in comments to SPP that the complaint quotes.

“Rto’s [regional transmission organizations] do not have any accountability to ratepayers … and incumbents have too much influence over the RTOs,” Paul Cicio, president and CEO of the Industrial Energy Consumers of America, told the Daily Caller News Foundation in a statement.

The coalition speaks for companies that consume electricity, but its members also include think tanks and “non-incumbent transmission developers,” according to the complaint.

Transmission rates are “the fastest growing part of consumer electricity bills,” the complaint states.

SPP’s rules let it hand a project straight to the local utility only if the project is “required to be in service within three years or less to address an identified reliability violation,” the complaint states. None of the four lines is scheduled to enter service before May 2029, according to the complaint.

One is a 239-mile line running from the Texas Panhandle into southeastern New Mexico. SPP said the line was needed by June 1, 2026, its December 2025 project report shows. That line is not scheduled to enter service before Nov. 18, 2030, according to the complaint.

The projects “have already been assigned and the Designated Transmission Owners are in the process of developing and/or constructing them,” SPP wrote in a Nov. 6 motion to FERC. (RELATED: Americans On The Hook After Data Center Transmission Line Cost Suddenly Doubles)

“There is no evidence Complainants will be harmed without Commission action before February 2027,” SPP wrote in the motion.

FERC closed an investigation into the exemption in 2020 after finding SPP still met its criteria, the grid operator noted in its motion.

The two groups waited nearly nine months after SPP’s board approved the designations to file, the grid operator argued in a Nov. 12 filing.

“SPP is aware of the complaint that has been filed at FERC regarding short-term reliability projects and is currently reviewing it,” the grid operator said in a statement to the DCNF.

It will keep following its tariff rules so the projects are “constructed in a timely manner to keep the lights on,” SPP said.

Xcel Energy, which owns Southwestern Public Service Company, did not respond to a request for comment. Oklahoma Gas and Electric (OG&E) did not provide a comment on the record.

The four projects would cost $3.78 billion, SPP’s report shows. About $2.37 billion of that is for a 315-mile line from central Oklahoma to northwest Louisiana.

FERC’s Order No. 1000 took away utilities’ first crack at building lines picked in regional plans, the commission’s summary states. It did not make regions take bids.

“Even a 20 percent reduction in the approximately $3.8 billion of proposed investment would represent $760 million in savings,” the Conservative Energy Network, which backs the complaint, wrote on Wednesday.

The group calls itself dedicated to free-market energy policy. It warned that such estimates “should not be interpreted as guaranteed savings for the projects at issue.”

OG&E offered to give up its return on equity on whatever it spends on the Oklahoma-Louisiana line beyond 20 percent above the estimate in SPP’s notice to construct, according to testimony from Jay Caspary of TransGrid Advisors, a witness for the complainants.

“Foregoing return on equity for costs 20% above a figure you get to name, with no outside competitive pressure to offer the lowest dollar amount possible, does not robustly incentivize aggressive cost reductions for customers,” Caspary wrote.

New Mexico’s Public Regulation Commission asked FERC to keep the cost of delay in mind. Drillers in the state’s slice of the Permian Basin still cannot hook their wells up to the local utility, so they run them on diesel and gas generators, the commission wrote on Wednesday.

For the New Mexico line, “speed to power is imperative,” the commission added. It said it “does not take the position that an extended construction schedule negates the reliability need itself” but also cautioned that “potential delay does not excuse noncompliance.”

The report blames fast load growth and weak ties to the rest of SPP. Southwestern Public Service’s expected load jumped from about 4,700 megawatts to 11,500 megawatts between the 2023 and 2025 planning cycles, nearly 150 percent, it shows.

More than 57,000 outage scenarios in SPP’s models for the area would not solve, which the report says could mean voltage collapse.

SPP later cut the area’s forecast by 11 percent to 20 percent, but the reliability concerns “remain largely unchanged,” the report states.

SPP’s board approved the four designations on Feb. 3. That same day it backed an effort “to maintain and improve the competitive bid framework,” meeting minutes show.

The groups are asking FERC to find that SPP broke its tariff. They also want all four lines put out for bid, according to the complaint.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by DAVID GANNON/AFP via Getty Images)

Despite calling on America to replace profitable energy standards and policies with environmentally friendly alternatives, the European Union (EU) is falling far short of its own green spending goals, with a deadline just weeks away, according to new European Commission figures.

Member countries have submitted only €113 billion in qualifying projects since the 2020 pledge. Of that amount, less than €90 billion has actually been financed through the sale of EU green bonds, joint debt created to fund the program, Politico reported Wednesday. (RELATED: Will The Blue Wave Be Followed By A Green Wave?)

When the pledge was launched to help member countries recover from the economic effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Commission said special green bonds would fund 30 percent of the €648 billion program. However, Commission data released on November 10 showed that only €86 billion worth of bonds had been issued, less than half the target.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen (C) delivers a speech during a debate on the conclusion of the European Council meeting of 18-19 December 2025, at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, eastern France, on January 21, 2026. (Photo by FREDERICK FLORIN / AFP via Getty Images)

The EU must issue and allocate more than €100 billion worth of green bonds by the end of December to meet its goal. A Commission spokesperson told Politico that meeting the target “depends on EU member states reporting sufficient eligible green expenditure.”

The spokesperson added that “green bonds will continue to be issued” into next year.

The EU has also overstated its spending on environmentally friendly projects, Politico reported, citing the European Court of Auditors. The watchdog examined 60 projects across seven member countries, representing nearly 90 percent of the union’s green spending, and found that spending was overstated by approximately 10 percent.

The watchdog described spending on green projects as “materially overstated” in eight of the 60 projects assessed. It also estimated that the EU had exaggerated green spending by almost 90 percent as of August 2025.

In one case, France classified the installation of a new gas-fueled heating system as green spending, according to Politico.

This photograph shows wind turbines in a wind farm in Villar de los Navarros, Zaragoza province in Spain on April 5, 2022. (Photo by CESAR MANSO/AFP via Getty Images)

Despite its own shortcomings, the EU has continued to criticize the U.S. over its climate policies. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told the union’s media arm, Euronews, last week that it is “deeply unfortunate” that the U.S. is appearing to ignore climate through its pollution, labeling it “one of the biggest hairy problems humanity is facing.”

“We don’t need denialism or hesitation. We need action,” Hoekstra continued. “And it is only fair that the ones who are most responsible also take most action.”

In January, President Donald Trump withdrew from the 1992 treaty that sought to have countries work with the United Nations to mitigate climate change.

At the time, the White House said the treaty promoted “radical climate policies, global governance, and ideological programs that conflict with U.S. sovereignty and economic strength.”

The decision prompted a response from European Commission Executive Vice-President Teresa Ribera, who said, “The White House doesn’t care about environment, health or suffer of people.”

Activists wearing masks of (L-R) French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Angela Merkel, China’s President Xi Jinping and President of the European Commission Jean-Claude Juncker hold up a banner reading “G19: Don’t Trump our Planet” as they stand next to a giant balloon of the Earth with a haircut alluding to US President Donald Trump in front of the Chancellery in Berlin on June 29, 2017. (Photo by JOHN MACDOUGALL/AFP via Getty Images)

European criticism of American climate policy predates Trump’s second term, including his decision to withdraw from the Paris Agreement in 2017 and again after returning to office in 2025.

Following the 2017 withdrawal, French President Emmanuel Macron said that Trump had “committed an error for the interests of his country, his people and a mistake for the future of our planet.” (RELATED: Trump Admin Keeps Michigan Coal Plant Open Into 2027 After Court Tossed Its First Order)

Trump’s 2025 withdrawal prompted less of an international response, but Hoekstra described the decision as a “truly unfortunate development.”

(Photo by Natalie Behring/Getty Images)

A bill moving through Congress would let nuclear developers skip permit hearings that nobody asked for.

Under the bill, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission would not have to hold a permit hearing unless someone asks for one. The House passed it Nov. 11, and the Senate passed the same change Nov. 19 as part of a broader permitting bill.

That goes for the licenses reactors need to operate, not just permits to build, the House Energy and Commerce Committee said.

TerraPower, which Jeffrey Epstein-tied billionaire Bill Gates helped found, got a construction permit from the commission in March for a reactor in Kemmerer, Wyoming, the company said. Dow has proposed putting four X-energy reactors at its site in Seadrift, Texas. Dow and X-energy won a permit for them Nov. 9. The companies still need an operating license and are preparing that application, they announced.

Holtec filed the first part of its permit application Dec. 31, 2025, for two small reactors at its Palisades site in Michigan, the American Nuclear Society reported. (RELATED: Reactor Permits Pile Up Under Trump As Democrats Prepare To Take Over Nuclear Oversight)

The University of Illinois has asked the commission for a permit to build NANO Nuclear Energy’s KRONOS microreactor, the American Nuclear Society reported. NANO has “no basis today to move the KRONOS construction date forward or quote a dollar saving” from the bill, CEO James Walker said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation.

“Affected parties would retain the right to request a hearing, and any hearing would use informal procedures,” Walker said of the bill.

X-energy, TerraPower, Holtec, Dow and the University of Illinois did not respond to the DCNF’s requests for comment. Aalo Atomics, another reactor developer, and the commission did not provide a comment on the record.

Since June 8, a commission policy has called for holding its required hearings early in a review, with the public invited to take part, the Federal Register shows.

The House bill passed by voice vote, congressional records show. Republican Virginia Rep. Morgan Griffith introduced it in September 2025.

The House Rules Committee is set to take up the Senate-passed permitting bill Nov. 30, the committee announced.
news.content:
(عکس از ناتالی برینگ/گتی ایماژ)
لایحه ای که از کنگره عبور می کند به توسعه دهندگان هسته ای اجازه می دهد از جلسات استماع مجوزی که هیچ کس درخواست نکرده است صرف نظر کنند. بر اساس این لایحه، کمیسیون تنظیم مقررات هسته ای مجبور نیست جلسه استماع مجوز برگزار کند مگر اینکه کسی درخواست کند. مجلس آن را در 11 نوامبر تصویب کرد و سنا نیز همان تغییر را در 19 نوامبر به عنوان بخشی از یک لایحه گسترده تر مجوز تصویب کرد. کمیته انرژی و بازرگانی مجلس نمایندگان گفت که این موضوع در مورد مجوزهایی است که رآکتورها برای کار نیاز دارند، نه فقط مجوزهای ساخت. داو پیشنهاد کرده است که چهار راکتور X-energy را در سایت خود در Seadrift، تگزاس قرار دهد. داو و ایکس انرژی در 9 نوامبر برای آنها مجوز گرفتند. آنها اعلام کردند که شرکت ها هنوز به مجوز بهره برداری نیاز دارند و در حال آماده سازی آن درخواست هستند. انجمن هسته ای آمریکا گزارش داد که هولتک اولین بخش از درخواست مجوز خود را در 31 دسامبر 2025 برای دو راکتور کوچک در سایت Palisades خود در میشیگان ارائه کرد. (مرتبط: در حالی که دموکرات ها برای نظارت بر هسته ای آماده می شوند، مجوزهای رآکتور در زمان ترامپ انباشته می شود) انجمن هسته ای آمریکا گزارش داد که دانشگاه ایلینویز از کمیسیون درخواست مجوز برای ساخت ریزراکتور KRONOS انرژی هسته ای نانویی کرده است. جیمز واکر، مدیر عامل شرکت، در بیانیه‌ای به روزنامه دیلی گفت که نانو هیچ مبنایی برای انتقال تاریخ ساخت کرونوس به جلو یا نقل قول پس‌انداز دلاری از صورت‌حساب ندارد.

Buoyed by the Democrats’ sweeping victories in the midterm elections, climate alarmists the world over are hoping the U.S. will soon return to what New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani might refer to as the “warm embrace of climate collectivism.”

The upheaval in U.S. politics coincided with this year’s U.N.-sponsored climate summit (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, a posh resort on the Mediterranean, complete with Roman-Ottoman architecture, five-star hotels, and inviting beaches. It is from these opulent surroundings that the world’s masses will be called on to make sacrifices to save the planet from manmade climate change. Ever mindful to cater to the creature comforts of its well-heeled attendees, it is worth noting that the U.N. never holds these things in places like Fargo in January.

Because the Trump administration has withdrawn the U.S. from the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, official Washington snubbed the proceedings. But delegations of American climate activists, which included Al Gore and John Kerry, made the trip, spreading the message that that Democrats’ majority status in the upcoming Congress portends well for all things green. Kerry assured the gathering that “people made climate change and its exigencies a voting issue.”

Joining delegates from 196 countries was Sweden’s Greta Thunberg. This is the first climate summit she has attended since the 2021 conclave in Glasgow, Scotland, where she dismissed world leaders’ promises to take decisive action as “blah, blah, blah.”

Greta had it right then, and this year’s talks were no exception. But instead of following the usual script of decrying the state of the planet and solemnly pledging to cut their countries’ emissions of greenhouse gases by a date certain, delegates reached no agreement, and the talks ended in total failure. (RELATED: The Climate Left Can’t Defend Its Own Agenda. Conservatives Haven’t Made Them Try)

The climate extravaganza in Turkey is a sideshow; the real action will be here at home. Once they ascend to majority status in Congress in January, Democrats will be under pressure from their green supporters, led by purveyors of wind turbines and solar panels, to roll back Trump’s rollback of Obama- and Biden-era climate initiatives. The theatrics will no doubt include CEOs of oil and gas companies being hauled before congressional committees and berated for the damage their industry is inflicting on the planet. Yet despite having comfortable majorities in the House and Senate, reimposing a green-energy transition on the country won’t be easy — at least for the two years remaining in Trump’s term.

For example, reinstating subsidies for wind and solar power and tax credits for purchasers of electric vehicles (EVs) — all phased out under Trump’s 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act — would easily pass the new Congress but would face a certain presidential veto, which Democrats will not be able to override. Similarly, Democrats could pass bills barring the administration from repealing Biden-era rules restricting emissions from coal- and natural gas-fired power plants, but this, too, would take veto-proof majorities they don’t have. The same fate awaits any legislation aimed at reimposing Biden-era restrictions and fees on methane emissions from natural gas drilling.

Bills could also target Trump’s scrapping of Biden-era fuel-economy standards that effectively mandated a national switchover from gasoline-powered vehicles to EVs. Here, too, Trump could use his veto pen to great effect. And even if such a bill somehow became law, EVs currently make up only 6.5% of new car sales. The driving public overwhelmingly rejects them.

All Trump climate/energy policies are already the target of lawsuits filed by environmental groups and blue-state attorneys general, but the litigation will drag on for years with an uncertain outcome.

Appropriations bills funding the government provide Democrats a more promising opportunity to influence spending priorities that could include restoring funds for green-friendly programs. Vetoing such measures would risk a government shutdown, something the White House may be reluctant to do. Another option is attaching “riders” to spending bills that bar agencies from taking certain actions. Riders, however, are subject to Senate filibusters, meaning Democrats would need 60 votes to get them passed (they will have 56 seats come January).

While divided government will keep both sides in check at the national level, the midterms increased the number of states where Democrats enjoy a trifecta (control of the governor’s office and both houses of the state legislature). And these states offer greener pastures for those seeking to tilt the energy playing field in favor of wind and solar power. In Pennsylvania, for example, the incoming chair of the House Energy Committee, Democratic state Rep. Elizabeth Fiedler, citing the “climate crisis,” told Inside Climate News she plans to move quickly on passing bills boosting infrastructure for renewable energy. This, she said, would promote affordability and stave off the threat of blackouts and brownouts.

Feeding the grid a steady diet of intermittent wind and solar power will only destabilize it, thereby increasing the chances of blackouts and brownouts. Contrary to John Kerry’s musings in Turkey, the midterms were not about the climate. The Iran war triggered a spike in fuel prices, lending credence to calls for “affordability.” And for that, unaffordable and unreliable green energy offers no solution.

Bonner Russell Cohen, Ph.D., is a senior policy analyst with the Committee for a Constructive Tomorrow (CFACT).

The views and opinions expressed in this commentary are those of the author and do not reflect the official position of the Daily Caller News Foundation.

(Photo by Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

Several incoming House Democrats are prepping for legislative and investigative actions, as well as symbolic, commemorative gestures, focusing on the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riots.

Following their 2026 midterm victory, Democrats returning to power on Capitol Hill want to keep the riots and President Donald Trump’s subsequent mass pardon of roughly 1,500 defendants in the spotlight during his final two years in office, Politico reported Friday.

Among other things, congressional investigative committees are recruiting staff from the pool of former Department of Justice (DOJ) prosecutors who handled Jan. 6 cases before being dismissed. Meanwhile, some lawmakers are reportedly drafting bills to legally prohibit the administration from using public money to compensate pardoned rioters.

The DOJ ditched a proposed “anti-weaponization” fund in June; however, Democrats want to pass a permanent statutory ban, according to Politico. (RELATED: Oh, Stop It!’: Todd Blanche Cuts Off Dana Bash’s Speculating How Trump’s Alaska Election Lawsuit Could Lead To Another Jan 6)

Democratic Maryland Rep. Jamie Raskin, who has become the figurehead of the Democratic Party’s lawfare campaigns against Trump and the GOP following the Jan. 6 riots, said their new efforts will ensure that “historical truth is respected and not lied about.”

“We want to see that the government is on the side of the police officers and their families and not on the side of the violent insurrectionists,” he told Politico.

Democrats will also consider a symbolic resolution to condemn Trump’s mass pardon, and plan to hold a formal observance for the riot’s upcoming sixth anniversary, Politico reported. It would be the first official House recognition of the riots since Democrats held a majority in 2022.

Democratic Massachusetts Rep. Jim McGovern told Politico he is excited to “make it clear what really happened and to push back against these revisionist theories that Donald Trump [and] the Republicans have put forward.”

During the riot, McGovern took over the Speaker’s chair after then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi was rushed off the House floor. He presided over the chamber as the riots unfolded, and was one of the last members of Congress to evacuate the House floor.

“Instead of working to improve the lives of Americans, Democrats want to continue their obsession with January 6th,” White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said in a statement to Politico. “President Trump will continue to deliver wins for the American people, including the most secure border in American history, decreasing … the cost of prescription drugs, and putting more money back into the pocketbooks of American workers.”

(Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

Republican Nebraska Sen. Deb Fischer’s spokesperson announced Friday that her late husband died by suicide.

Fischer’s family initially believed that her late husband, Bruce, died peacefully at their home on Sunday at the age of 75, but further investigation found that he took his life, a spokesperson for Fischer announced on X. The Nebraska senator first announced her husband’s passing in a Monday statement.

“There has been a sad update in the death of Senator Fischer’s husband, Bruce,” Fischer’s spokesperson said. “Initially, it was believed that Bruce passed peacefully at home. Upon further investigation, it was learned that Bruce chose to end his life. The family is deeply grateful for the recent outpouring of sympathy for their loss, and asks for understanding in this time of mourning. There will be no further comment and no other details will be provided.” (RELATED: Republican Nebraska Sen. Deb Fischer Attends Elite DC Party Hosted By Major Gay Dating App)

A spokesperson for the office of Senator Deb Fischer issued the following statement today: There has been a sad update in the death of Senator Fischer’s husband, Bruce. Initially, it was believed that Bruce passed peacefully at home. Upon further investigation, it was learned that Bruce chose to end his life. The family is deeply grateful for the recent outpouring of sympathy for their loss, and asks for understanding in this time of mourning. There will be no further comment and no other details will be provided.

Fischer and her late husband were married for 54 years. In her initially announcement, Fischer referred to Bruce as her “partner in life, my greatest source of strength, and the heart of our family.

“Our family is heartbroken by his passing, but we find comfort in the life we shared with him,” Fischer said in a Monday statement. “I will cherish the decades we spent building a family in the Nebraska Sandhills. Above all, Bruce was a loving husband, a devoted father and grandfather, a man of faith and a rancher. We sincerely appreciate the prayers, kindness, and support extended to our family during this difficult time.”

The Nebraska senator met Bruce at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, according to her Senate profile. They married in 1972 and raised their three sons on their family ranch in Valentine, Nebraska.

Republican Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen and Republican Nebraska Sen. Pete Ricketts expressed their condolences over the passing of Fischer’s husband.

“Suzanne and I are keeping Sen. Fischer and her family in our thoughts. We share our prayers as she deals with this great personal loss,” Pillen said in a Monday statement.

“Bruce left his mark on this world through his love for family, his faith, and his ranch,” Ricketts said. “Susanne and I send our deepest condolences to Deb, the entire Fischer family, and all their loved ones during this difficult time. The Fischer family is in our prayers.”

Footage from January 2025 showed Bruce appearing to decline to shake hands with then-Vice President Kamala Harris as his wife was being sworn in.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Vernon Yuen/Nexpher Images via Getty Images)

Nvidia chips under U.S. export controls turned up at a Shanghai data center tied to Jensen Huang’s alleged affair partner.

Two Chinese companies allegedly installed Nvidia Blackwell processors at a Shanghai data center connected to Alice Huang, the former CEO of Megaspeed and reported affair partner of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to a Bloomberg report.

".. The submissions reveal for the first time that Nvidia’s Blackwell processors found their way into a Chinese data center that has ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed." @business $NVDA https://t.co/EfqmsVzQCh

Documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November indicate that the equipment at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, one of Nvidia’s most powerful data center systems, Bloomberg reported. (RELATED: Trump Says Investigation Cleared Nvidia CEO. Todd Blanche Won’t Say If DOJ Opened Criminal Probe Into Him.)

Shanghai Shuoyao reportedly used the hardware as collateral to secure a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to lender filings reviewed by Bloomberg.

A second company, Shanghai Kezhan, which is controlled by a Tokyo-based parent company, also listed a GB200 server at the facility in documents submitted to secure a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a financing company wholly owned by a Shanghai government agency, according to the report.

The GB200 server also relies on Nvidia’s Blackwell chips.

The filings offer the first documented indication that Nvidia’s Blackwell processors had reached a Chinese data center with ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed.

The advanced processors were, until recently, Nvidia’s most powerful data center chips and have been prohibited from being exported to China without a U.S. government license. (RELATED: GOP Senator Says Trump’s Nvidia Intervention Sets ‘Dangerous Precedent’)

President Donald Trump has publicly opposed allowing Nvidia’s most advanced processors to be shipped to China, while CEO Jensen Huang has previously argued that the systems would be difficult to smuggle because of their sheer size.

A standard GB300 NVL72 rack stands roughly two meters tall, weighs more than 1,500 kilograms (3,300 pounds) and contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips and 36 Grace processors — making it roughly the scale of an oversized refrigerator.

Despite those logistical challenges, Nvidia and its recently reinstated CEO have faced mounting scrutiny over the alleged diversion of the company’s advanced chips to China through a black market that U.S. officials believe is worth billions of dollars. (RELATED: Trump Was ‘Totally Involved’ In Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Return, White House Confirms)

It remains unclear how the GB300 rack reached Shanghai Shuoyao or the specific data center, which local media reports say was designed to house as many as 800,000 servers. Bloomberg traced the rack’s serial number through a public warranty database, identifying Taiwan-based Gigabyte Technology Co. as its manufacturer.

Gigabyte assembles Nvidia chips into servers and racks, and the database’s listed model matched a GB300 NVL72 system produced by the company.

Such equipment can pass through multiple intermediaries and distribution networks before reaching data centers, with some hardware eventually ending up in China after being initially sold to buyers in countries where exports are permitted.

Bloomberg alleges it contacted Gigabyte with the rack’s serial number to determine its original buyer and sale date, but the company declined to provide those details, citing corporate policies.

A spokesperson told the outlet that Gigabyte conducts business in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and subjects transactions to internal compliance requirements, according to Bloomberg.

Shanghai Shuoyao, which obtained the GB300 rack and used it as loan collateral, operates at the data center connected to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker.

Shuoyao has significant business ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under U.S. investigation over allegations of smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

The company, which had not responded to Bloomberg’s inquiries over the past year, acknowledged in a rare public statement this month that it provides services to Megaspeed, describing the relationship as “limited to ordinary commercial cooperation.”

Megaspeed previously showed investors a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project in 2024, identifying it as its largest data center and describing it as a facility in an unnamed country, according to the Friday report by Bloomberg.

Importantly, Bloomberg also reported that it found no evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted Nvidia hardware to the data center. (RELATED: Both Sides Of Congress Upset Trump Put Thumb On Scale To Reinstate Jensen Huang As Nvidia CEO)

The Singapore-based company has denied wrongdoing in connection with the U.S. investigation, pushing back against a separate Bloomberg report in a statement posted to LinkedIn. The company wrote that the report contained “misleading information and incorrect insinuations,” including suggestions of possible illegal activity.

Megaspeed statement on a Bloomberg report.

Megaspeed also warned it would not rule out legal action to protect its reputation and hold Bloomberg accountable for what it called the article’s misleading claims.

The Trump administration’s Department of Commerce added Megaspeed to a U.S. trade blacklist this month, citing a significant risk that the company was involved in diverting advanced chips to China.

(Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images)

Republican Rep. Maria Salazar is firing back at immigration hardliners, claiming they’re using the word “amnesty” as a “cheap word trick.”

Salazar defended her efforts to overhaul the U.S. immigration system in a Thanksgiving Day post Thursday that echoed her calls for lawmakers to debate the issue without resorting to accusations of “amnesty.” (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: White House Scrambles After Trump Again Floats Amnesty Deal With Democrats)

The South Florida Republican representative has become one of the GOP’s most prominent voices advocating for immigration reform, responding to a post from Oklahoma Republican Gov. Kevin Stitt on X: “Governor, I AGREE! The word AMNESTY is used to shut down one of the most serious conversations as a nation we should have: how to reform our immigration system. Immigration goes far beyond immigrants and illegals.”

Governor, I AGREE! The word AMNESTY is used to shut down one of the most serious conversations as a nation we should have: how to reform our immigration system. Immigration goes far beyond immigrants and illegals. It’s about the economy, affordability, national security, economic growth. It affects ALL Americans. Legitimate disagreements, and labels are no substitute for good policies. Let’s debate this issues without resorting to name-calling and cheap word tricks. Even on the toughest issues, we can disagree with DIGNITY and respect. That’s the American way! Thank you, @GovStitt for being courageous, a voice of reason, and not shying away from a national conversation we desperately need to have.

The congresswoman argued that immigration policy extends beyond border enforcement, saying it affects “the economy, affordability, national security, economic growth” and “ALL Americans.”

“Legitimate disagreements, and labels are no substitute for good policies. Let’s debate this issues (sic) without resorting to name calling and cheap word tricks,” Salazar added.

She also thanked Stitt for his willingness to engage in the debate, invoking the concept of “DIGNITY,” a central theme of her immigration legislation.

“Even on the toughest issues, we can disagree with DIGNITY and respect. That’s the American Way! Thank you, Governor Stitt, for being courageous, a voice of reason, and not shying away from a national conversation we desperately need to have,” she wrote on X.

Salazar has emerged as a vocal advocate for working across party lines on immigration legislation, particularly as President Donald Trump has signaled an interest in reaching a deal with Democrats.

But that renewed push has also raised questions among Republican skeptics of immigration reform about what such an agreement would entail, including whether any deal could move forward without granting some form of amnesty and what concessions Republicans might have to make.

Stitt made a similar argument in an X post Wednesday promoting his op-ed published in The Oklahoman, titled, “Stitt to Vance: Stop using ‘amnesty’ to block immigration reform.”

“Amnesty” has become the weapon of choice for ending a conversation America needs. I’ve never called for it. I’ve called for states to be partners with Washington on legal visas, with a secure border and enforcement behind them. Read more in my op-ed today:

“‘Amnesty’ has become the weapon of choice for ending a conversation America needs. I’ve never called for it. I’ve called for states to be partners with Washington on legal visas, with a secure border and enforcement behind them. Read more in my op-ed today,” Stitt wrote.

Salazar’s DIGNIDAD legislation (Dignity Act) would establish a pathway to legal citizenship for illegal immigrants already in the United States while also seeking to strengthen border security, curb illegal immigration, and overhaul the asylum system to make it more efficient.

Salazar, who introduced the legislation, has also criticized Vance’s position on immigration reform. She previously argued that Trump’s immigration policies had gone “too far” in a September campaign advertisement. (RELATED: Trump-Endorsed Congresswoman Trashes His Immigration Policy In Scathing Ad)

Following the 2026 midterm elections, in a Nov. 4 post on X, Vance pointed to frustration among some 2024 Trump voters over the war in Iran as one factor behind Republican losses, while warning that establishment Republicans could use the coming months to push for amnesty.

One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we’re going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us." Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026. There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were: 1) End the war 2) Focus on cost of living/inflation 3) Put America First 4) Change our relationship to Israel Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.) In the next few months, there’s going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I’m open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there. I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

Vance argued that pursuing such a policy would mislead voters who supported Trump’s immigration agenda.

He acknowledged that Trump was open to adjustments in immigration enforcement, including shifting more attention toward businesses that employ illegal workers. Vance also cautioned that Republicans advocating for amnesty were “lying to you,” according to his post on X.

Salazar’s legislation gained 16 new co-sponsors as of Nov. 16, bringing the total to 55, including 20 Republicans. (RELATED: Maria Salazar Brags About Amnesty Bill Surpassing Necessary Co-Sponsors)

The Daily Caller reached out to Salazar for comment on how her proposed immigration reforms differ from amnesty but did not receive a response before publication.

فرماندار، من موافقم! کلمه عفو برای بستن یکی از جدی ترین گفتگوهایی که به عنوان یک ملت باید داشته باشیم استفاده می شود: چگونه سیستم مهاجرت خود را اصلاح کنیم. مهاجرت بسیار فراتر از مهاجران و افراد غیرقانونی است. این در مورد اقتصاد، مقرون به صرفه بودن، امنیت ملی، رشد اقتصادی است. همه آمریکایی ها را تحت تاثیر قرار می دهد. اختلاف نظرهای مشروع و برچسب ها جایگزینی برای سیاست های خوب نیستند. بیایید بدون توسل به نامگذاری و ترفندهای کلمات ارزان در مورد این موضوع بحث کنیم. حتی در سخت‌ترین مسائل، می‌توانیم با حیثیت و احترام مخالفت کنیم. این روش آمریکایی است! با تشکر از شما، @GovStitt برای شجاعت

news.originalContent:
هم‌زمان با هفته بسیج، در پیامی که رسانه‌های ایران به مجتبی خامنه‌ای، رهبر جمهوری اسلامی، نسبت داده‌اند، بر ضرورت تحول در مأموریت‌های این سازمان و گسترش فعالیت آن در بخش‌های مختلف جامعه تأکید شده است.

در این پیام، تحقق شعار «هر ایرانی، یک بسیجی» یکی از اهداف دوره جدید عنوان شده است.

در متن کتبی منسوب به رهبر جمهوری اسلامی آمده است: «سازمان بسیج باید تحول و تولدی جدید را تجربه نماید. این سازمان باید با استفاده از ملت بعثت‌یافته، نسخه‌های پیشرفته‌تر و جدیدتری از بسیج پیشین را تنظیم و مدیریت کند.»

مجتبی خامنه‌ای از زمان تصدی این پست هنوز در انظار عمومی ظاهر نشده است.

مجتبی خامنه‌ای در پیامش همچنین از حاضران درتجمعات حکومتی که «یاران پرچم به‌‌ دستِ شبها و روزهای میادین و خیابان‌ها» خوانده و اعضای پویش «جان‌فدا» به‌عنوان بخشی از ظرفیت بسیج نام برده و خواستار استفاده از آنها برای حل مشکلات شده است.

تأکید بر گسترش فعالیت بسیج، پیش از این نیز در حکم انتصاب حسین طائب به ریاست این سازمان مطرح شده بود. در حکمی که مرداد ۱۴۰۵، منتشر شد، بر «تقویت شبکه اطلاعات مردمی» تأکید شده بود. با این هدف که بسیج برای مقابله «مردم‌پایه با تهدیدها» آماده و تقویت شود.

این تاکیدها در کنار تصدی حسین طائب، از چهره‌های باسابقه اطلاعاتی و امنیتی نزدیک به مجتبی خامنه‌ای به ریاست بسیج، توجه‌ها را به احتمال گسترش نقش اطلاعاتی و امنیتی این سازمان در دوره جدید جلب کرده است.

حسین طائب پیش از این در سال‌های ۱۳۸۷ و ۱۳۸۸ فرمانده بسیج بود. پس از آن به مدت ۱۳ سال ریاست سازمان اطلاعات سپاه پاسداران را بر عهده داشت اما در سال ۱۴۰۱ از این سمت کنار گذاشته شد. بازگشت او به رأس یکی از مهم‌ترین نهادهای زیرمجموعه سپاه، در شرایطی صورت گرفت که جمهوری اسلامی با پیامدهای جنگ و افزایش نگرانی‌ها از نارضایتی‌های داخلی روبه‌روست.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

بر این اساس هفته گذشته، حسین طائب از اجرای «سند تحول راهبردی» این نهاد به منظور افزایش دامنه فعالیت این سازمان در عرصه‌های مختلف خبر داد.

او روز ۲۸ آبان در جمع بسیجیان گفت این سند به تأیید رهبر جمهوری اسلامی رسیده و یکی از محورهای آن «طراحی الگوهای جدید سازماندهی برای مقابله با تهدیدهای نرم، امنیتی و دفاعی» است.

در میان اهداف اعلام‌ شده این برنامه، «تقویت اشراف اطلاعاتی محله‌محور» نیز قرار دارد. رویکردی که به گفته مقام‌های بسیج قرار است با مشارکت مردم در شناسایی «تحرکات مشکوک و اقدامات ضد امنیتی» دنبال شود.

یکی از مصادیق این برنامه، سازماندهی داوطلبان در قالب پویش «جان‌فدا» است.

هدف از راه‌اندازی‌ آن، آموزش‌های نظامی و عقیدتی برای جذب نیرو در حمایت از نظام و مشارکت در فعالیت‌های دفاعی و بازدارنده خوانده شده است.

به گفته علی کوثری، معاون آموزش سازمان بسیج،  تا کنون ۶۰ پایگاه آموزش نظامی مرتبط با طرح جان‌فدا فعال شده‌اند و قرار است مراکز آموزشی دیگری نیز از جمله در کنار برخی اماکن تاریخی و فرهنگی مانند تخت جمشید، ارگ بم، زیگورات و آرامگاه فردوسی برپا شوند.

اعضای این پویش در تجمعات حکومتی حضور قابل توجهی دارند. روز ۲۷ شهریور، گروهی از حامیان نظام در تجمع «جان‌فدایان» در محدوده میدان امام حسین تا خیابان انقلاب تهران راهپیمایی کردند. حسین طائب در این مراسم گفت که داوطلبان برای «دفاع همه‌جانبه» آماده می‌شوند.

گسترش فعالیت بسیج در حوزه آموزش محدود به مراکز نظامی نیست. این سازمان در همکاری با وزارت آموزش و پرورش، در قالب برنامه‌هایی همچون «نوجوان مبارز» و «نو+میدان»، حضور نیروهای نظامی را در کلاس‌های درس و فضاهای آموزشی بیشتر کرده است.

یکی دیگر از برنامه‌های بسیج، طرحی با عنوان «دستیار محلی» است که به گفته حسین طائب از دوم آذر در سراسر ایران اجرا شده است.

در این طرح، بسیج با محوریت مساجد و امامان جماعت، «افراد توانمند و فعال هر محله و همچنین نیازهای ساکنان» را شناسایی می‌کند. این داده‌ها قرار است با استفاده از هوش مصنوعی سازماندهی شوند.

مقام‌های بسیج هدف این طرح را تسهیل دسترسی مردم به خدمات و انتقال بخشی از فعالیت‌های اداری و اجتماعی به محله‌ها عنوان کرده‌اند. اما شیوه جمع‌آوری و نگهداری اطلاعات، و نهادهایی که به آنها دسترسی دارند، مشخص نیست.

این نهاد از یک سو به دنبال شناسایی ظرفیت‌های اجتماعی محله‌هاست و از طرف دیگر بر مشارکت مردم در شناسایی تحرکات مشکوک تأکید می‌کند. معلوم نیست این دو حوزه چگونه از یکدیگر تفکیک می‌شوند.

در جریان اعتراضات دی ماه سال گذشته، نهادهای امنیتی با استفاده از دوربین‌های کنترل ترافیک شهری، هویت گروهی از معترضان را شناسایی کردند. ناظران می‌گویند با ثبت اطلاعات مردم هر محله نگرانی‌هایی از احتمال استفاده از آنها برای نظارت بر شهروندان و شناسایی مخالفان و منتقدان وجود دارد.

تقویت شبکه اطلاعات مردمی در ساختار بسیج، پیش از این هم در قالب سازوکارهای مختلف دنبال شده است.

در خرداد ۱۴۰۴، ستاد خبری اطلاعات بسیج از شهروندان خواست مواردی مانند تصویربرداری از مراکز حساس و تردد‌ خودروهای مشکوک را به این نهاد گزارش کنند.

همچنین در برخی برنامه‌های بسیج، تکمیل بانک اطلاعاتی محله‌ها، تشکیل هسته‌های اطلاعاتی در پایگاه‌ها و اجرای گشت‌های اطلاعاتی معروف به  «گشت‌های رضویون» در دستور کار قرار گرفت.

تأکید تازه حسین طائب بر «اشراف اطلاعاتی محله‌محور» می‌تواند نشانه تلاش برای تقویت  چنین ساز و کارهایی برای مواجهه با بحران‌های داخلی و خارجی باشد.

از نشانه‌های این راهبرد، بنا به گزارش رسانه‌ها و نهادهای حقوق بشری، فعالیت ایست‌های بازرسی در خیابان‌ها، گشت‌ محلات و تجمعات شبانه حامیان حکومت بعد از اعتراضات دی ماه گذشته و حملات آمریکا و اسرائیل به ایران است.

به تازگی محسن هرمزی، معاون حمل‌ونقل و ترافیک شهرداری تهران، بازرسی بدنی و تلفن‌های همراه مسافران مترو در تهران را هم تایید کرد و به وبسایت  رویداد۲۴ توضیح داد که «این برخوردها با توجه به ضرورت‌های امنیتی» انجام می‌شود.

سازمان بسیج مستضعفین در آذر ۱۳۵۸ به فرمان روح‌الله خمینی؛ بنیانگذار جمهوری اسلامی و با هدف تشکیل نیرویی مردمی برای دفاع از انقلاب تأسیس شد. این سازمان در جریان جنگ ایران و عراق، داوطلبان برای حضور در  جبهه‌ها را تأمین می‌کرد، اما پس از جنگ و در دوران رهبری علی خامنه‌ای، دامنه فعالیتش به حوزه‌های سیاسی و امنیتی هم گسترش یافت.

بسیج که زیرمجموعه سپاه پاسداران است، در بیش از چهار دهه گذشته به شبکه‌ای‌ گسترده در محله‌ها، مدارس و دانشگاه‌ها و نهادها تبدیل شده، ردیف بودجه مستقل دارد و در سرکوب اعتراضات مردمی از جمله در سال‌های ۱۳۸۸، ۱۳۹۸ و ۱۴۰۱ نقشی محوری داشته است.

تأکید بر گسترش فعالیت‌های بسیج در شرایطی مطرح می‌شود که جمهوری اسلامی با مجموعه‌ای از چالش‌های داخلی و خارجی روبه‌روست.

جنگ و آسیب‌هایی که به ساختار نظامی و امنیتی ایران وارد شد، مقامات را به بازنگری در ظرفیت‌های دفاعی و شیوه سازماندهی نیروها سوق داده است.

به علاوه، فشارهای اقتصادی و نارضایتی‌های اجتماعی از مهم‌ترین چالش‌های پیش روی جمهوری اسلامی به شمار می‌روند.

مصطفی تاجزاده، فعال سیاسی زندانی، با اشاره به تشدید فشارهای اقتصادی، افزایش قیمت کالاها و ادامه صدور احکام سنگین علیه معترضان و مخالفان، درباره احتمال شکل‌گیری اعتراضات سراسری هشدار داده است.

این زندانی سیاسی گذارطلب در دیدار با همسرش، فخرالسادات محتشمی‌پور، اجرای حکم ۷۴ ضربه شلاق پرستو احمدی و چهار نفر از عوامل گروه هنری «کنسرت کاروانسرا»، اعدام معترضان، مصادره اموال مخالفان و صدور احکام سنگین زندان را از جمله عواملی دانسته که به گفته او ظرفیت افزایش خشم عمومی را دارند.

با وجود چنین هشدارهایی، به نظر راهکار مقامات،  گسترش شبکه بسیج ‌برای کنترل و در رصد تحولات داخلی است.

از نگاه ناظران، تحولات تازه بخشی از تلاش برای افزایش نقش بسیج در تثبیت قدرت است. نقشی که در دوره جدید رهبری می‌تواند برای سازماندهی نیروها و مواجهه با بحران‌های داخلی و خارجی اهمیت بیشتری پیدا کند.

در این پیام، تحقق شعار «هر ایرانی، یک بسیجی» یکی از اهداف دوره جدید عنوان شده است.

در متن کتبی منسوب به رهبر جمهوری اسلامی آمده است: «سازمان بسیج باید تحول و تولدی جدید را تجربه نماید. این سازمان باید با استفاده از ملت بعثت‌یافته، نسخه‌های پیشرفته‌تر و جدیدتری از بسیج پیشین را تنظیم و مدیریت کند.»

مجتبی خامنه‌ای از زمان تصدی این پست هنوز در انظار عمومی ظاهر نشده است.

حسین طائب پیش از این در سال‌های ۱۳۸۷ و ۱۳۸۸ فرمانده بسیج بود. پس از آن به مدت ۱۳ سال ریاست سازمان اطلاعات سپاه پاسداران را بر عهده داشت اما در سال ۱۴۰۱ از این سمت کنار گذاشته شد. بازگشت او به رأس یکی از مهم‌ترین نهادهای زیرمجموعه سپاه، در شرایطی صورت گرفت که جمهوری اسلامی با پیامدهای جنگ و افزایش نگرانی‌ها از نارضایتی‌های داخلی روبه‌روست.

مصطفی تاجزاده، فعال سیاسی زندانی، با اشاره به تشدید فشارهای اقتصادی، افزایش قیمت کالاها و ادامه صدور احکام سنگین علیه معترضان و مخالفان، درباره احتمال شکل‌گیری اعتراضات سراسری هشدار داده است.

این زندانی سیاسی گذارطلب در دیدار با همسرش، فخرالسادات محتشمی‌پور، اجرای حکم ۷۴ ضربه شلاق پرستو احمدی و چهار نفر از عوامل گروه هنری «کنسرت کاروانسرا»، اعدام معترضان، مصادره اموال مخالفان و صدور احکام سنگین زندان را از جمله عواملی دانسته که به گفته او ظرفیت افزایش خشم عمومی را دارند.

با وجود چنین هشدارهایی، به نظر راهکار مقامات،  گسترش شبکه بسیج ‌برای کنترل و در رصد تحولات داخلی است.

از نگاه ناظران، تحولات تازه بخشی از تلاش برای افزایش نقش بسیج در تثبیت قدرت است. نقشی که در دوره جدید رهبری می‌تواند برای سازماندهی نیروها و مواجهه با بحران‌های داخلی و خارجی اهمیت بیشتری پیدا کند.

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.

news.originalContent: Senior government officials admit that Israel's public opinion in the international community "has never been worse." According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten.  Follow Ynetnews on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | TikTok >> More stories: IDF releases name of fallen soldier in West Bank terror attack UN chief in Rafah crossing says world 'seen enough' of Gaza war Two Air Force pilots reminisce about their murdered brothers: 'There's no room for pain in the air' The officials added that the intensity of accusations made against Israel only increases, and attempts to equate Hamas's actions in Israel are being made, with allegations accusing IDF soldiers of sexually harassing Palestinian prisoners. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

news.originalContent: Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guards warned anti-government protesters of "decisive" action if unrest over gasoline price hikes do not cease, state television reported on Monday. The warning appeared to hint at a looming crackdown on protests that flared nationwide in response to an official announcement on Friday of gasoline rationing and price hikes of at least 50 percent. "If necessary we will take decisive and revolutionary action against any continued moves to disturb the people's peace and security," the Guards said in a statement carried by state media.
news.content: تلویزیون دولتی روز دوشنبه گزارش داد که سپاه پاسداران قدرتمند ایران به معترضان ضد دولتی هشدار داد که اگر ناآرامی ها بر سر افزایش قیمت بنزین متوقف نشود، اقدام «قاطعانه» خواهند کرد. به نظر می‌رسد این هشدار به سرکوب اعتراض‌هایی که در سراسر کشور در واکنش به اعلام رسمی روز جمعه مبنی بر سهمیه‌بندی بنزین و افزایش حداقل 50 درصدی قیمت‌ها شعله‌ور شد، اشاره می‌کند. سپاه پاسداران در بیانیه‌ای که توسط رسانه‌های دولتی منتشر شد، گفت: «در صورت لزوم، در برابر هرگونه اقدام مستمر برای برهم زدن آرامش و امنیت مردم، اقدام قاطع و انقلابی خواهیم کرد».
